title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple: Time Expressions
grammarTitle: Present Perfect vs Past Simple — Choosing the Right Tense
grammarNote: Это одна из самых важных — и самых путающих — тем в английском. Present Perfect используется, когда нет конкретного времени в прошлом (или важен результат, а не момент). Past Simple используется, когда ЕСТЬ конкретное время или момент в прошлом. Ключевые слова-подсказки помогают правильно выбирать время.

grammarExtra.title: Present Perfect signals — no specific past time

rows.example: "Have you EVER been abroad?" / "I've NEVER met the president."
"She's ALREADY applied." / "Have you finished YET?" / "Not yet."
"I've JUST arrived." = a moment ago, very recently.
"Have you seen him RECENTLY?" / "She's been busy LATELY."
"SINCE 2020" (start point) / "FOR three years" (duration).
"She's done well SO FAR." / "What have you achieved UP TO NOW?"

grammarExtra.title: Past Simple signals — specific past time

rows.example: "I saw him YESTERDAY." (completed in the past, specific time)
"LAST week / LAST summer / LAST year." → always Past Simple.
"She won IN 2022." / "He arrived IN July." → specific time.
"Three weeks AGO." / "Two hours AGO." → Past Simple.
"WHEN I was a child..." / "WHEN did you go?" → Past Simple.
"AT 7 p.m. / AT midnight / AT that moment." → Past Simple.

grammarExtra.title: The PP → PS pattern (very common in conversation)

rows.example: "Have you BEEN to Shymkent?" (life experience, no time)
"Yes, I WENT there in 2021." (now I give a specific time)
✗ "Did you go there?" → ✅ "Have you been there?" (then follow with PS if yes)
"I've seen that film." → "Really? When did you see it?" → "I saw it last Friday."
✅ "I saw him yesterday." — "yesterday" → Past Simple!
✅ "Have you ever been to Almaty?" — "ever" → PP!
✅ "She won in 2022." — "in 2022" → Past Simple!
✅ Use one or the other: "I've already seen it." OR "I saw it yesterday."

grammarTip:
Главный секрет выбора времени:
① Есть ли конкретное время в предложении? (yesterday, last week, in 2022, ago) → Past Simple
② Нет времени, но есть ever/never/already/yet/just/since/for? → Present Perfect
③ Паттерн разговора: PP для общего вопроса → PS для деталей с временем.

💡 Тест: мысленно спроси "КОГДА?"
→ "I've been to Almaty." Когда? Непонятно = Present Perfect ✅
→ "I went to Almaty last summer." Когда? "Last summer" = Past Simple ✅

⚠️ НИКОГДА не используй PP с: yesterday, last night/week/year, in 2022, ago, at that moment.

exercises.instruction: Choose Past Simple or Present Perfect.
exercises.hint: "last summer" = specific past time → Past Simple. "Kamila went last summer." ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose Past Simple or Present Perfect.
exercises.hint: No specific time given → Present Perfect. "She has won two championships." ✅

exercises.text: "I have seen him yesterday" is correct.
exercises.hint: ✅ "I saw him yesterday." — "yesterday" = specific past time → ALWAYS Past Simple!

exercises.text: "___ you ever ___ (be) abroad?" — General life experience question.
exercises.hint: "ever" + life experience (no specific time) → Present Perfect. "Have you ever been abroad?" ✅
"in 2022" = specific past year → Past Simple. "I read the novel in 2022." ✅ (read: /red/)

exercises.text: "Have you been to Shymkent?" — "Yes, I ___ there in 2021."
exercises.hint: PP (general question) → PS when specific time is given. "Yes, I went there in 2021." ✅
"already" → Present Perfect. "She's already applied." ✅ (already goes BEFORE the past participle)

exercises.text: "He ___ (win) the regional championship three years ago."
exercises.hint: "ago" = specific past time → Past Simple. "He won the championship three years ago." ✅

exercises.text: "___ you finish the exercise yet?" — "No, I haven't."
exercises.hint: "yet" → Present Perfect question. "Have you finished yet?" ✅ (not "Did you finish yet?")

exercises.instruction: Choose Present Perfect or Past Simple.
exercises.hint: "since" = start point to now → Present Perfect. "I've known her since secondary school." ✅

opts: She has won the championship in 2022.
She has won the championship in 2022 last year.
exercises.hint: "in 2022" = specific year → Past Simple. "She won in 2022." ✅

exercises.text: "I ___ (just / arrive) at the library. I'm looking for Amir."
exercises.hint: "just" → Present Perfect. "I've just arrived." = a moment ago, very recently. ✅

questions.text: "I went to Almaty last year." — Why Past Simple?
opts: "Last year" is a specific past time
questions.correct: "Last year" is a specific past time
questions.hint: "last year / last week / yesterday / in 2022" → ALWAYS Past Simple.

questions.text: "Have you ever been to Bishkek?" — Why Present Perfect?
questions.hint: "ever" signals a PP question about life experience. No specific past time mentioned.

questions.text: "She ___ (win) the championship ___ ago." Use correct tense.
questions.hint: "ago" = specific past time → Past Simple. "She won the championship three years ago." ✅

opts: I have seen him last night.

questions.text: "She ___ (apply) for the master's programme." (she just did it, no time given)
questions.hint: No specific time → PP. "She has applied." ✅ Add "already": "She's already applied."

questions.text: "Have you finished the book?" — "Yes, I finished ___ ."
questions.hint: "Last night" = specific time → PS: "Yes, I finished it last night." ✅ (Question: PP. Answer: PS because specific time.)

questions.text: "He ___ (play) volleyball since he was a child."
questions.hint: "since" = PP. "He's played volleyball since he was a child." ✅

questions.text: "___ you ever ___ (meet) a famous person?" — General experience.
questions.hint: "ever" → PP. "Have you ever MET a famous person?" ✅

questions.text: "I've ___ arrived at the station." — Which word fits here?
questions.hint: "just" = very recently, a moment ago. "I've just arrived." = PP + just ✅

questions.text: "She has won in 2022." — What is wrong?
questions.hint: "in 2022" = specific year → Past Simple. ✅ "She WON in 2022."

questions.text: "Have you seen the new film?" — "No, not ___ . I'll watch it tomorrow."
questions.hint: "yet" goes at the end of PP negative questions and answers. "Not yet." = "No, I haven't yet." ✅

questions.text: "She's been playing volleyball since she was nine." — "since" means:
opts: from a starting point in the past until now
questions.correct: from a starting point in the past until now
questions.hint: "since" = from a starting point (she was nine) until NOW. Still playing now! ✅

opts: I have seen it last year.
questions.hint: PP question → PS answer (when specific time is given). "I saw it last year." ✅

questions.text: "She's ___ applied for the scholarship — before the deadline."
questions.hint: "already" = before expected time, action is done. "She's already applied." ✅ (position: before participle)

questions.text: "He ___ (win) three awards in his career so far."
questions.hint: "so far" = from beginning until now (no specific time) → PP. "He's won three awards so far." ✅

questions.text: Which sentence correctly uses PP signal words?
questions.hint: "ever" = PP signal. "Have you ever TRIED...?" ✅ Others have specific past time signals → should be PS.
